title: A suitable microsurgical method for obstructive cholestasis in the rat
protocol: Anesthetize the rat with i.p. ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (12 mg/kg).
Disinfect the skin with Chlorhexidine-alcohol (0.5%) antiseptic solution.
Make a midline abdominal skin and muscle incision (about 5 cm long), to expose the xyphoid process.
Retract bilaterally the cut laparotomy wall using two-curved mosquito forceps so that they hold open the peritoneal cavity, thereby exposing the liver.
While gently pulling down the middle lobe with a saline-moistened cotton tip, use a curved microsurgery scissors to cut the falciform ligament.
Using a moistened gauze tip, lift the middle and left lateral lobe and hold them against thorax.
Gently pull towards the left the duodenum with a saline-moistened cotton tip to visualize the hepatic hilum.
Retract the duodenum and the small intestine loops towards the left and cover them with a saline moistened gauze to maintain the hepatic hilum exposed.
Place the rat under an operating microscope at x 6-10 magnification.
Free the common bile duct from surrounding peritoneum and connective tissue using two small micro-tweezers with a 45º angle.
Free the common bile duct from hepatic artery and portal vein in the segment located between the hepatic hilum and the beginning of the intrapancreatic portion of the bile duct.
Place a 5-0 silk thread around the common bile duct using microdissection forceps.
Ligate the common bile duct doubly close to the beginning of its intrapancreatic portion.
Transect the common bile duct between the two ligatures.
Maintain a proximal ligature of the common bile duct with a length of 4-5 cm for later handling.
Dissect upwards the common bile duct using two small micro-tweezers with a 45º angle to identify the first lobular biliary branch.
Dissect the biliary branch of the caudate lobe and isolate it from arterial and portal branches using a moistened cotton tip and small micro-tweezers.
Doubly ligate the lobular biliary branches of the caudate lobe with 6-0 silk sutures, placing the first ligature close to the parenchyma and the second close to the common bile duct.
Transect the biliary lobular branch of the caudate lobe between the two ligatures using microsurgery curved scissors.
Gently pull the ligated common bile duct to the left and dissect the second biliary branch belonging to the right lateral lobe using angled micro-tweezers.
Identify the arterial and portal branches of the right lateral lobe and free the biliary branch from them using a moistened cotton tip and small micro-tweezers.
Doubly ligate the lobular biliary branches of the right lateral lobe with 6-0 silk sutures, placing the first ligature close to the parenchyma and the second close to the common bile duct.
Cut the biliary lobular branch of the right lateral lobe between the two ligatures using microsurgery curved scissors.
Dissect upwards the biliary tract of the middle and left lateral lobes with micro-tweezers.
Pull the ligated common bile duct to the right, holding it with a micro-tweezers, to tract the lobular biliary branch of the left lateral lobe.
Identify the arterial and portal middle and left lateral lobular branches.
Free the biliary branch of the left lateral lobe from the identified branches using a moistened cotton tip and small micro-tweezers.
Ligate the lobular biliary branches of the left lateral lobe with 6-0 silk sutures, placing the first ligature close to the parenchyma of the left lateral lobe.
Place the second ligature close to the drainage of the left middle lobe duct into the hilar biliary tract.
Dissect the left middle lobe biliary branch carefully using angled micro-tweezers and a moistened cotton tip.
Avoid injuring the hepatic parenchyma during dissection of the lobular biliary branch.
Prevent injury to the portal branch of the left middle lobe during dissection.
Doubly ligate the lobular biliary branch of the left middle lobe using 6-0 silk sutures.
Place the first ligature as close as possible to the parenchyma of the left middle lobe.
Position the second ligature close to the drainage of the right middle lobe duct into the hilar biliary tract.
Dissect the right middle lobe biliary branch carefully using angled micro-tweezers and a moistened cotton tip.
Doubly ligate the lobular biliary branch of the right middle lobe using 6-0 silk sutures.
Place the first ligature as close as possible to the parenchyma of the right middle lobe.
Position the second ligature close to the drainage of the middle lobe duct into the hilar biliary tract.
Use the microsurgery curved scissors to cut the biliary lobular branches of the left lateral lobe between two ligatures.
Use the microsurgery curved scissors to cut the biliary lobular branches of the left middle lobe between two ligatures.
Use the microsurgery curved scissors to cut the biliary lobular branches of the right middle lobe between two ligatures.
Check the tightness of all biliary stumps; ensure that bile only flows from the resected biliary branches.
Place the middle and left lateral lobes into their anatomical location using moistened cotton swabs.
Carefully return intestinal loops to the abdominal cavity.
Administer 1ml dextrose-saline or saline intraperitoneally.
Close the aponeurotic layer of the abdominal wall muscle with a continuous running suture using a 3-0 poliglactin 910 suture and needle holder.
Close the skin abdominal incision using a continuous running suture with a 4-0 silk suture and needle holder.
Wipe the skin surrounding the suture with chlorhexidine.
Administer buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg subcutaneously.
Place the animal on a warming pad for recovery for 15 minutes.
